title: Part Twenty-Three: How the Bible Was Made

sections.brief: The documents that sorted the books, c.180-1546: Irenaeus's four gospels and the Gospel of Truth; the Muratorian fragment (Wisdom, Apocalypse of Peter, Hermas not public, forged Pauline letters); Origen's doubts and Serapion's Gospel of Peter; Eusebius's four shelves and Rome doubting Hebrews; Athanasius 367; Carthage 419 sending its list to Boniface to confirm; Rome 382/Gelasian dispute; Jerome's Prologus Galeatus and Solomon preface, and his Judith-at-Nicaea report; Cajetan/Seripando, Florence 1442, Trent 8 April 1546 (24-15-16), Sixtus of Siena 1566. Figures: time

Books left out with who excluded each and in what document (Irenaeus, Muratorian, Origen, Serapion, Eusebius, Athanasius, Jerome, Gelasian Decree's 62 entries incl. 'Leptogenesis'/Jubilees and church writers, Trent's appendix); counts: 27 of 38 in Eusebius's catalogue kept, 4 of 21+ named gospels, 1 of 5 revelations, ~46 Nag Hammadi titles mostly unnamed in any list; what exclusion meant (reading in church, warning, anathema; no destruction order; the documented burning order was for Arius's writings); verdict on 'suppressed most of the books'. Figures: compare (ledger); stats

Protestant 66 (Luther 1522/1534, Anglican Articles, Westminster 1646, Bible societies 1820s), Catholic 73 (Florence 1442, Trent 1546, appendix books), Eastern Orthodox ~76 (Septuagint, 1 Esdras, 3 Macc, Ps 151, Prayer of Manasseh, 4 Macc appendix; Trullo 692, Jerusalem 1672 not binding on all), Ethiopian 81 (narrower canon, unique books, Fetha Negest 81-but-73, broader canon +9); Peshitta 22 NT, Armenian Revelation c.1200; what the comparison shows. Figures: compare
